instruction:
Fix `packages/excalidraw/actions/actionProperties.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. 1) yarn test:typecheck: actionProperties.tsx(438,3): error TS2322: Type '"changeHighlightColor"' is not assignable to type 'ActionName'. The ActionName union is defined in packages/excalidraw/actions/types.ts, which is OUTSIDE this run's write contract and must not be edited: do not register a new action name. Keep the Highlight behaviour without a new ActionName (e.g. route the highlight through actionChangeBackgroundColor's perform with a distinguishing value such as { highlightColor }, or apply it via updateData of the existing action); keep exporting what other files import, or keep an exported alias that still works. 2) actionProperties.tsx(647,15): error TS2322: Type 'readonly string[]' is not assignable to type 'readonly [string, string, string, string, string]' (topPicks for the Highlight ColorPicker). 3) actionProperties.tsx(657,21): error TS2339: Property 'actionManager' does not exist on type 'AppClassProperties' (use the PanelComponent's updateData instead of app.actionManager.executeAction). 4) Regressions in existing tests that passed before this run (yarn test:app --watch=false packages/excalidraw/tests/stickyNotes.test.tsx): 'sticky notes > editing > routes a top pick to the label and the sticky default while editing a note' -> expected getElement(label.id).strokeColor '#1e1e1e' to be '#e03131' (stickyNotes.test.tsx:604); 'sticky notes > editing > offers the note's background while editing its label and colors the note with it' -> expected getElement(note.id).backgroundColor '#ffdf6b' to be '#fcc2d7' (stickyNotes.test.tsx:653). Cause: the WYSIWYG editor calls editable.select() when it opens, so the whole text is 'selected' and colour picks are routed to a text range instead of the element. Fix: only treat the selection as a range when 0 < selectionStart < selectionEnd is a strict sub-range, i.e. NOT when it covers the whole originalText (start === 0 && end === originalText.length) — then apply to the whole element exactly as before; and never route actionChangeBackgroundColor to a highlight for sticky-note labels (the note background behaviour must be unchanged). Existing tests must pass unchanged.
